sheets.title: Guptas and Harsha (319 – 647 CE)
sheets.intro: Gupta kings, Navaratnas, science, art, government; Harsha, Bana, Hiuen Tsang.

keys.name: Rise of the Guptas
keys.hook: Sri – Ghato – Chandra I – Samudra – Chandra II – Kumara – Skanda

rows.v: Feudatories of the Kushanas; filled the gap after Kushanas and Satavahanas
Iron ore of central India and south Bihar; Byzantine silk trade
Gupta era 319 – 320 CE (Chandragupta I); Vallabhi era is the same
Smaller than Mauryan; north united over a century

keys.name: Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha

rows.v: c. 240 – 280; founder; title Maharaja; called "Adhiraja" in Poona plates of Prabhavatigupta; home maybe Bengal

traps: Sri Gupta founded; Chandragupta I was the first emperor

keys.name: Chandragupta I
traps: Chandragupta I (319 CE) ≠ Chandragupta Maurya (322 BCE)

keys.name: Samudragupta

rows.v: "Napoleon of India" (V.A. Smith); policy of war ("blood and iron")
Prayag (Allahabad) Prashasti on an Ashokan pillar – Harisena (Sandhivigrahika, Kumaramatya, Mahadandanayaka); Sanskrit champu; also Eran inscription
12 kings captured, freed, restored (grahana – moksha – anugraha) – Mahendragiri of Pishtapura (Pithapuram), Hastivarman of Vengi, Kubera of Devarashtra, Ugrasena of Palakka, Vishnugopa of Kanchi
Meghavarman of Sri Lanka – leave to build a Bodh Gaya monastery
Veena player, archer, tiger slayer, Ashvamedha

traps: Northern kings annexed; southern kings freed
Hastivarman of Vengi (Salankayana) and Vishnugopa of Kanchi (Pallava) were beaten

keys.name: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya

rows.v: Devichandraguptam (Vishakhadatta) – killed brother Ramagupta and a Shaka king; married Dhruvadevi
Ended Western Kshatrapas (Rudrasimha III, c. 409) – Malwa, Gujarat, west ports
First Gupta silver coins; lion-slayer gold
Mehrauli iron pillar ("Chandra"); Udayagiri caves (Varaha panel); Sanchi inscription of Amrakardava
Fa-Hien (Faxian) c. 399 – 411 – Fo-kuo-ki; does not name the king

traps: Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II) ≠ Hiuen Tsang (Harsha) ≠ I-Tsing (after Harsha)

rows.v: Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram (Agnimitra Shunga hero), Vikramorvashiyam; Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Meghaduta, Ritusamhara
Vararuchi, Vetala Bhatta, Ghatakarpara, Shanku, Kshapanaka

keys.name: Mehrauli iron pillar

rows.v: Barely rusted for 1,500+ years – Gupta metallurgy
To Mehrauli (Qutb complex), Delhi – the notes credit Firoz Shah Tughlaq

traps: Mehrauli = iron, Chandragupta II; Allahabad = stone, Samudragupta

rows.v: Pushyamitras attacked late in his reign
Beat the first Huna wave and the Pushyamitras – Bhitari pillar (Ghazipur, UP)
Junagadh inscription – Sudarshana repaired by Chakrapalita, son of governor Parnadatta

keys.name: Later Guptas and the Hunas

rows.v: Purugupta, Kumaragupta II, Buddhagupta, Narasimhagupta Baladitya, Bhanugupta, Vishnugupta (last, c. 540 – 550)
Huna chief – took west and central India
His son; Shaiva; persecuted Buddhists; capital Sakala
Bhanugupta's time – first record of Sati
Pushyabhutis (Thanesar), Maukharis (Kannauj), later Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, Maitrakas

traps: Eran: Samudragupta inscription + Bhanugupta Sati record 510

rows.v: Bhukti (province – Uparika) → Vishaya (district – Vishayapati) → Vithi → Grama
Nagarashreshthi (banker), Sarthavaha (caravan trader), Prathama Kulika (chief artisan), Prathama Kayastha (chief scribe)
Cash at first, then land grants – feudal tendency; governors strong (Aulikaras of Malwa)
Shrenis – own rules, banks for endowments; seals at Vaishali, Bhita
Tax-free, hereditary grant to Brahmins with revenue rights
Kshetra (farmed), Khila (waste), Aprahata (forest), Vasti (homestead), Gopata Sarah (pasture)

keys.name: Gupta coins and trade

rows.v: King-Queen (CG I); veena, archer, Ashvamedha, tiger (SG); lion slayer (CG II); peacock (KG I)

traps: First gold coins = Indo-Greeks; most gold = Kushanas; finest gold = Guptas

keys.name: Gupta science

rows.v: Born 476; Aryabhatiya 499 at Kusumapura; place value, zero; earth rotates on its axis; eclipses by shadows
Panchasiddhantika (505 – 5 systems: Surya, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha, Paitamaha); Brihat Samhita; Brihat Jataka
Later – Brahmasphuta Siddhanta (628), not Gupta court

traps: Aryabhata said rotation, not revolution round the sun

keys.name: Gupta art and temples

rows.v: Dashavatara, Deogarh (first shikhara, panchayatana); Bhitargaon (brick, Kanpur); Sanchi temple 17 (flat roof); Tigawa; Nachna (Parvati)
Udayagiri (Varaha); Ajanta later caves – Vakataka patronage
Sarnath Buddha; Sultanganj Buddha – 2.3 m copper

traps: Sultanganj Buddha is copper, not stone

keys.name: Gupta society and faith
keys.hook: Golden age, but not for all

rows.v: Vaishnavas; Garuda emblem; Bhagavatism, avatars, Gita
Outside towns; struck wood to warn (Fa-Hien)
Peace, mild punishment, vegetarian, no spies

keys.name: Pushyabhutis and Harsha’s family

rows.v: Rajyavardhana – beat Devagupta of Malwa; killed by Shashanka of Gauda (Karnasuvarna)
Rajyashri – married Grahavarman Maukhari of Kannauj (killed by Devagupta); rescued in the Vindhya forest from sati

traps: Devagupta killed Grahavarman; Shashanka killed Rajyavardhana

keys.name: Harshavardhana

rows.v: Born 590; king at 16 in 606 (Harsha era); died 647 with no heir
Beat Shashanka with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa; held Punjab, central India; Bengal, Bihar, Odisha; Vallabhi's Dhruvasena II beaten, then son-in-law
By Pulakeshin II on the Narmada, 618 – 619 CE (Aihole inscription)
Siladitya (Hiuen Tsang); "Sakalottarapathanatha" (lord of all north – Aihole)
Shaiva till c. 631; then Mahayana; honoured all faiths
Ratnavali (Udayana; early Holi mention), Priyadarshika, Nagananda (Buddhist – Jimutavahana)

traps: Harsha lost to Pulakeshin II in 618 – 619, not 630

keys.name: Banabhatta

rows.v: Prose life of Harsha (akhyayika); first historical biography in Sanskrit; names Pushyamitra's coup too

traps: Bana wrote prose; Harsha wrote the plays

rows.v: Nalanda the top university; Prayag, Kannauj rising; Pataliputra, Vaishali declined; Sanskrit of the learned; he was robbed (law and order not perfect)
Kanchi (Narasimhavarman I, 642); praised Pulakeshin II's rule
c. 643; honoured Hiuen Tsang; Mahayana; kings, monks attended
Mahamoksha Parishad every 5 years; treasury given as alms; Hiuen Tsang at the 6th one; Buddha, Surya, Shiva worshipped on different days
Revenue of about 100 villages (Hiuen Tsang's biographer)
In monasteries; Vedas oral; Sanskrit; age about 9 – 30
Palas; Vikramashila (Dharmapala); destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji c. 1193

keys.name: Harsha’s government

rows.v: Avanti (foreign affairs, war), Simhanada (army chief), Kuntala (cavalry), Skandagupta (elephants)
Mimamsakas as judges; trial by ordeal; life term instead of death after Buddhism

traps: Bhaga = share of crop; Hiranya = cash

rows.v: Minister Arunashva attacked Chinese envoy Wang Xuance; Wang came back with Tibetan, Nepali troops and beat him
Regional kingdoms; tripartite struggle for Kannauj later
Last great north Indian king before Turkish rule
